alerts.title: DTG Contraindicated Due to Hyperglycemia
alerts.message: Guidelines state that a patient with high glucose should not initiate or transition to DTG. The patient's fasting glucose is 118 mg/dL (6.55 mmol/L), which exceeds the guideline threshold of >6.95 mmol/L (125 mg/dL) for high fasting glucose. She has multiple risk factors: age ≥30, family history of DM, BMI ≥25 kg/m², and hypertension. DTG is a reported cause of hyperglycemia in non-diabetic adults. However, weight gain and family history are also contributing factors.

evidence.recommended_action: Do not initiate or transition to DTG. Consider ATV/r or maintain on EFV, and monitor blood glucose.

alerts.title: Missing Glucose Monitoring Plan
alerts.message: Guidelines require glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year after initiating or transitioning to DTG. The patient transitioned to DTG 18 months ago. There is no clinician plan today to address her impaired fasting glucose (118 mg/dL) and HbA1c in the pre-diabetic range (6.1%). Acanthosis nigricans and significant weight gain since starting DTG are clinical signs of insulin resistance.

evidence.recommended_action: Implement guideline-recommended glucose monitoring and assess for diabetes management.

alerts.title: Obesity and Metabolic Syndrome
alerts.message: Patient BMI is 32.4 kg/m² (Obese class I per WHO classification), increased from 25.6 kg/m² 18 months ago. Waist circumference is 96cm. Guidelines classify BMI ≥30 as obese. This significant weight gain coincides with DTG initiation. She also has dyslipidemia (high LDL, low HDL, high triglycerides) and new-onset hypertension (BP 138/88 mmHg). DTG-associated weight gain is a known phenomenon, though diet and lifestyle are also factors.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for DTG-associated weight gain and metabolic syndrome. Provide lifestyle counseling and consider regimen review.
